children: Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. signed a multiyear agreement with OpenAI and G42 to use artificial intelligence across its oil and gas operations, expanding its use of the technology from reservoir analysis to production planning, refining and trading.

The agreement, announced Monday at the ADIPEC energy conference in Abu Dhabi, will make Adnoc the first energy company to deploy OpenAI's Frontier platform, the state-owned oil giant said. Financial terms weren't disclosed.

The technology will initially focus on field development planning, combining data from thousands of wells and reservoirs with cost and investment considerations. Adnoc said it expects the system to reduce the time needed to prepare complex development plans from months to hours.

A second application will connect production, refining, logistics and trading operations, using AI to forecast crude supply, demand, prices and margins and assess the commercial impact of operational decisions.

The agreement builds on Adnoc's existing investment in artificial intelligence. In March 2025, AIQ, an AI company partly owned by Adnoc, announced a three-year, $340 million contract to deploy AI technology across the oil producer's upstream operations, covering more than 28 producing fields.
Adnoc has also reported operational improvements from earlier AI systems, including a reduction of about half in unplanned shutdowns and a one-third decline in planned upstream maintenance.

The latest deal expands an existing relationship between OpenAI and United Arab Emirates firm G42. The companies announced plans last year for a 1-gigawatt AI data center in Abu Dhabi, with an initial 200-megawatt phase expected to be completed by the end of 2026, The Wall Street Journal previously reported. The project is part of a broader push by the U.A.E. to become one of the world's biggest funders of AI companies and infrastructure--and a hub for AI jobs.
The new systems will use OpenAI's models and Adnoc's industrial data, running on G42's U.A.E.-based computing infrastructure, with human oversight of major decisions.

The partnership was among four agreements announced Monday between OpenAI and Abu Dhabi entities, covering energy, government services and investment management, according to the Abu Dhabi Media Office.
News Corp, owner of The Wall Street Journal and Dow Jones Newswires, has a content-licensing partnership with OpenAI.
